target_customer: Small teams and builders who need backends and automations without writing server code
problem: Setting up APIs, databases and workflows for an MVP or internal tool takes engineering time that small teams lack.
business_model: SaaS subscription for a low-code API and workflow builder

founders.name: Mike Mahlkow
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Constantin Schreiber
education: Dropped out of college, school not named

exit.reason: Lumos acquired Fastgen's automation technology (workflow builder), not the whole company; terms undisclosed. Fastgen said it would focus remaining resources on AI projects.

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual API and workflow builder with a hosted Postgres database and prebuilt integrations is standard platform engineering with some hard parts around scale and reliability.

defensibility.rationale: Customers who build backends on the platform face some lock in, but Zapier, Retool and others offered close substitutes and the product was easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not clear that incumbents copied it. The technology was bought by Lumos in December 2024.

market_need_then: Low code and no code backend tools were in demand among small teams; the YC page lists use for MVP and internal tool backends and GTM, ops and marketing automation.

branding.domain_note: Uses an exact fastgen.com per Product Hunt and the Launch HN post.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and developer friendly; the tagline is Webflow for the Backend.

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post in mid 2023 and a Product Hunt listing; one reviewer praised it. No merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name fits the speed pitch and the exact .com helped, but searches showed little press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Fastgen was a low-code API and workflow builder from founders who had earlier run Blair, a YC S19 company. In December 2024 Lumos bought its workflow builder technology and Fastgen said it would put its remaining resources into AI projects. The sources give no sale price and no funding amount from a primary source, so the result cannot be called a clear success or failure.
notes: Directory lists Active, while Lumos bought the automation technology in December 2024; the company may continue in AI work. Aggregators claim about 500 thousand dollars raised from Y Combinator, Rebel Fund or 468 Capital with conflicting investors, so it is unverified and no round is recorded. The YC page says Blair raised over 100 million dollars, which looks inconsistent and is unverified. No dated competitor sources near mid 2023 were found, so the list is empty. Completeness pass: convertible note dated 2023-01-01 recorded from CB Insights with no amount; the round rests on a single database. Lumos press release (2024-12-09) confirms the technology acquisition but gives no funding figures.
